title: Scope, consent and trade boundaries
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Electrical licences and credentials (last updated 23 June 2026); NSW Government, Plumbing, draining and gasfitting (last updated 31 July 2026); NSW Government, Minor trade work (last updated 23 June 2026); Queensland Building and Construction Commission, When you need a QBCC licence (last reviewed 11 August 2021); SafeWork NSW, Class B asbestos removal licence (published 12 November 2025; last modified 12 March 2026); WorkSafe Queensland, Asbestos licences (no date shown); Victorian Government, Unlicensed asbestos removal (asbestos.vic.gov.au; 'Updated' label, no date shown); Energy Safe Victoria, Safely installing photovoltaic (PV) systems (reviewed 15 April 2025).
audience: Handyman and property maintenance workers, including those taking work from owners and property managers
learningOutcomes: Explain the difference between having the skill to perform a task and having the authority to perform it.
Classify a requested task as within scope, outside scope, or referred to a licensed trade.
Record the agreed scope, the approver and any variation before work starts.

instruction.heading: Skill is not authority
instruction.body: A handyman job is usually small: hanging a fixture, patching a wall, adjusting a door, or replacing a worn part on something that is not part of a regulated system. The work is often ordinary and you may be able to do it well. Ability does not answer the first question, which is whether the person asking holds the authority to approve the work and whether the task is one a non-licensed worker may carry out at that property. Authority comes from the owner or from a property manager acting for the owner, and it is set out in the written work order. Which state or territory law applies depends on where the property sits, and the state positions checked for this course appear under trade boundaries below. Your own competence does not create either form of authority.

instruction.heading: Scope, consent and variations
instruction.body: Before you touch anything, read the work order and confirm three things in writing: what will be done, where it will be done, and who approved it. Identify the occupant as well as the owner. A tenant or other occupant may need to agree to access and may need to be present. If the request changes during the job, stop that part, record the new request, and obtain approval from the person who holds authority before you perform it. Verbal changes made on site are the most common source of disputes about who approved what. A short written message from the approver is enough, provided it names the change and the date.

instruction.heading: Trade boundaries and referral
instruction.body: Some work belongs to licensed trades, and the state position decides where the line sits, so check it for your state before you rely on it. Wiring jobs in New South Wales need a licence or certificate whatever their price, and the NSW electrical page sets no dollar threshold (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). Plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences in New South Wales cover those trades at any price, by category (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). The NSW minor trade work threshold is more than $5,000 across labour and materials, GST included (minor trade work page, last updated 23 June 2026). In Queensland, plumbing, drainage and gasfitting need a QBCC licence at any dollar value (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). Handyman work valued at $3,300 or less needs no QBCC licence when it is not electrical or plumbing and no occupational licence applies; that page is dated 2021 and does not say how labour, materials or GST are counted (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). A lesson saying a task is ordinary handyman work does not confirm that the task is lawful for you in the state where you work. When a task touches a licensed trade, your job is to stop, record the boundary, and refer it to a person who holds the correct licence.

instruction.heading: Recording the decision
instruction.body: Each job needs a short record: the agreed scope, the approver, the date, any task refused or referred, and the reason. A refusal or referral that is recorded protects the client and the worker, because it shows the boundary was considered and not ignored. Keep the record with the work order. Do not rewrite it later to fit what was done.

instruction.heading: Everyday tasks and state requirements
instruction.body: The everyday tasks in this course are taught to every learner, so you can recognise them on a job, scope them properly and know when to stop. Hanging a fixture, patching a wall, adjusting a door and replacing a worn part are ordinary handyman tasks, but a state can restrict any of them once the work touches a regulated trade. Each task is taught here for recognition and where the state note confirms the work is allowed, and each one must be checked against the state note before you do it. In New South Wales, you must have an electrical licence or certificate before you can do any electrical wiring work, regardless of the cost of the work (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). In New South Wales, plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences cover those trades at any price, by category (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). In Queensland, the QBCC handyman exemption does not cover electrical or plumbing work, a QBCC licence is needed for drainage, plumbing and gas fitting work at any value, and the QBCC page directs electrical questions to the Electrical Safety Office, so confirm the Queensland electrical rule with that office before you start (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). In Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria states that installation and maintenance of PV systems are required to be carried out by licensed electrical workers (page reviewed 15 April 2025). The sources for this lesson do not state the Victorian rule for other fixtures, or any plumbing rule for Victoria. They also do not cover South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory, so treat a task that touches wiring, plumbing, drainage or gas in those states as a referral until the state regulator confirms the position.

procedure: Read the work order and confirm the property address, the owner or manager who approved it, and the occupant contact.
Write down each requested task on a single list, one line per task.
Mark each task as within scope, outside scope, or referred to a licensed trade, and give the reason in one sentence.

Check the state position for any task that touches wiring, gas, plumbing, drainage or structure, using the official pages in the references. For asbestos-containing material, check the state rules: New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria.
Stop before starting any task that is outside scope or referred. Tell the approver in writing and wait for a decision.
For a variation, record the request, the approver and the time before any work on it begins.
Close the record with the outcome of each task: done, refused, referred or pending.

workedExamples.situation: A property manager asks you to replace a ceiling light fitting, and to add two new power points in the same room. The manager says the owner has agreed by phone.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What can you accept, what must you refer, and what must be in writing before you start?
workedExamples.reasoning: Adding power points involves new electrical wiring. In New South Wales, wiring work needs a licence or certificate whatever the price (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), so the new power points must be referred to a licensed electrical worker. Replacing a light fitting also involves electrical work, so treat it as a referral. The phone agreement is not a written approval, so ask for written confirmation before anything is started, and record the referral.

equipmentAndPpe: Written work order or written message naming the scope and the approver
Owner, manager and occupant contact details
Site access details, recorded and kept private
Photo record device, used only with consent
The licence matrix for the state where the job is performed

commonErrors.error: Starting work on a verbal agreement.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask for a written work order or a written message that names the scope, the approver and the date before you start.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a small job falls outside licensing rules.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the official page for the trade. In New South Wales, wiring applies whatever the price (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), and so do plumbing and gasfitting (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). In Queensland, the $3,300 figure is a building-work threshold with exceptions, so it is not a general pass for every trade (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021).

commonErrors.error: Accepting a variation during the job without recording it.
commonErrors.prevention: Pause the variation, write it down, and get approval from the authorised person before performing it.

commonErrors.error: Treating an everyday task as licence-free in every state.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state note for each task. In New South Wales, wiring needs an electrical licence or certificate at any cost (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), and in Queensland the QBCC handyman exemption does not cover electrical or plumbing work (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021).

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wiring work in New South Wales needs a licence or certificate whatever the price, and the NSW electrical page sets no dollar threshold. The page excludes electrical equipment operating at not more than 50 volts AC or 120 volts ripple-free DC (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026). This lesson does not grant that licence and does not authorise wiring work.

Plumbing, draining and gasfitting in New South Wales need a licence or certificate at any price, by category (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). In Queensland, these trades need a QBCC licence at any dollar value (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker for either.

The NSW minor trade work page (last updated 23 June 2026) sets a licence threshold of more than $5,000 across labour and materials, GST included, but it does not settle the handyman position. On the Queensland QBCC page (last reviewed 11 August 2021), a handyman needs no licence while the value is no more than $3,300, provided the work is not electrical or plumbing and does not need an occupational licence. Confirm with the relevant regulator before relying on any of these positions.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or authority to do regulated work, and it does not change any state position.

Everyday tasks in this course are restricted in some states. Where a state restricts the work, the state note in the everyday tasks section sets the requirement, and the task must not be treated as licence-free in that state.

qualityStandard: The scope, the approver and the date are recorded before any work starts.
Each requested task is classified as within scope, outside scope or referred, with a one-sentence reason.
Every variation is approved in writing before it is performed.
documentationEvidence: Work order or written message with scope and approver
Variation record with the date, the change and the approver
Referral note naming the licensed trade and confirming the client was told
summary: A skill does not create authority to perform a task.
Confirm the scope and the approver in writing before starting, and record every change.
Refer any task that touches a licensed trade, and check the matrix for the state before relying on a boundary.

knowledgeChecks.question: A tenant asks you to replace a power point that is warm to the touch. Which response is correct?
options: Replace it yourself because the job looks simple and quick to finish for the tenant
Stop, do not work on the power point, and refer the task to a licensed electrical worker
Tighten the terminals and say nothing to the owner about the warmth you noticed
Remove the cover and check the wiring with your own tester before deciding

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about licensing for regulated trade work is correct after this lesson?
options: It gives you a trade licence in most states once you finish the course and pass the exam
It replaces the state licence for any trade once it has been signed off by the trainer
It is training evidence only and does not grant a licence or authority to do regulated work
It is valid for any trade once a supervisor signs the record in the workplace

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for extra work that is outside the written scope. What should you do?
options: Do it because the client is present on site and is asking for it in person right now at the job
Do it now and invoice the difference later, once the job has been finished, checked and signed off by the client
Ask a neighbour whether it is acceptable, since they know the house and the owner well enough to say
Record the request, pause that part, and obtain written approval from the authorised person before doing it
